items.content_excerpt: $MSFT $NVDA The rotation wasn't out of tech. It was out of the picks and shovels. Microsoft and the cloud software majors rallied Wednesday while the AI hardware supply chain got sold — memory down about 7%, optical suppliers down around 9%, Nvidia off 3%. The trigger wasn't demand. It was the growing fear that US data-center construction faces new permitting friction, especially in Texas, where the incoming governor pledged a pause. If the buildout's bottleneck shifts from chips to permits, the whole supplier ladder reprices. Buying the hardware dip, or rotating into the software that's already monetizing?

items.content_excerpt: $SPCX $TSLA a fundamental regulatory misunderstanding: large institutions do not file Form 4s when selling down a typical investment position. 1. The Regulatory Disconnect: Form 4 vs. Form 13F/13D • Form 4 is for Insiders Only: • Institutional Whales are Exempt: Large asset managers, hedge funds, and private wealth allocators who own 1%, 2%, or 5% of the outstanding float are not insiders. Their selling is quietly conducted via block trades and dark pools, and it will only become visible to the public months down the road through Schedule 13D/G amendments or quarterly Form 13F filings. 2. The Gwynne Shotwell Friday Donation Narrative The mention of Gwynne Shotwell donating &quot;one share per child on Friday&quot; is a classic retail distraction Even if an insider executes a charitable donation the volume of such an action is a drop in the ocean compared to the 47.5 million shares of TSLA and 135.4 million shares of SPCX that washed through the tape today.

items.title: Apple is cutting employee AI spending allowances as part of a broader cost-control effort, even as it seeks to make artificial intelligence
items.content_excerpt: Apple is cutting employee AI spending allowances as part of a broader cost-control effort, even as it seeks to make artificial intelligence central to its operations. According to Bloomberg, the company reduced daily AI spending limits for some engineers last month to $200 from $300 and is considering further cuts to as little as $100. Some non-engineering teams already face $100 daily limits, which could fall to $25 for certain groups. Employees requiring higher budgets will need senior management approval. The allowances cover token consumption across AI models, with more advanced systems and complex tasks such as software development and debugging generating higher costs. Internal reactions have been mixed: while some employees rarely used their previous $300 allowances, others view the cuts as part of a broader cost-reduction initiative that could signal potential layoffs. $AAPL

items.title: $MSFT $NVDA The rotation wasn't out of tech. It was out of the picks and shovels. Microsoft and the cloud software majors rallied Wednes
items.content_excerpt: $MSFT $NVDA The rotation wasn't out of tech. It was out of the picks and shovels. Microsoft and the cloud software majors rallied Wednesday while the AI hardware supply chain got sold — memory down about 7%, optical suppliers down around 9%, Nvidia off 3%. The trigger wasn't demand. It was the growing fear that US data-center construction faces new permitting friction, especially in Texas, where the incoming governor pledged a pause. If the buildout's bottleneck shifts from chips to permits, the whole supplier ladder reprices. Buying the hardware dip, or rotating into the software that's already monetizing?

items.title: Congress Changed Hands. Did the $RKLB Thesis Change? - Part 2 What stays in place unless explicitly changed: - Electron commercial contracts
items.content_excerpt: Congress Changed Hands. Did the $RKLB Thesis Change? - Part 2 What stays in place unless explicitly changed: - Electron commercial contracts: Booked launches aren’t reset by the election. - Existing SDA satellite and HASTE awards: Remain awarded, subject to funding, options and termination clauses. Total contract value doesn’t mean every dollar is already funded. - Previously approved missile-defense funding: The election itself doesn’t repeal it; this is program funding, not money guaranteed to RKLB. What changes or could change: - Additional Golden Dome funding: Once the new Congress takes office, approval requires agreement with Democratic majorities. That doesn’t automatically mean less funding. - Future SDA, HASTE and military launch awards: Funding levels, timing and priorities could shift. - NASA projects: Congress could resist proposed science cuts, potentially preserving opportunities for RKLB’s launches, spacecraft and components.

items.title: $RKLB Congress Changed Hands. Did the $RKLB Thesis Change? I wouldn’t lower expectations for RKLB just because Congress changed hands. Democ
items.content_excerpt: $RKLB Congress Changed Hands. Did the $RKLB Thesis Change? I wouldn’t lower expectations for RKLB just because Congress changed hands. Democrats winning doesn’t automatically mean less spending on satellites, hypersonic testing or military launches. Golden Dome funding will require a different set of negotiations, but we need to see actual budget decisions before calling that a setback. Meanwhile, Electron has commercial customers to serve, and existing defense contracts give Rocket Lab work to deliver, although those awards aren’t immune to funding changes. There’s political uncertainty here, but that alone isn’t evidence the business has weakened. For me, the bigger questions remain the same: - Can Electron keep increasing its launch cadence? - Can Rocket Lab deliver its satellite contracts at healthy margins? - And can it get Neutron flying? Those are the developments that would change my view of the business.

items.content_excerpt: $RKLB $RKLB: Fundamentals Are Strong, Liquidity Is Rising. Valuations Will Follow. We’re still in a very different environment than in 2022, when monetary conditions were tightening aggressively. As Stanley Druckenmiller famously said, “It’s liquidity that moves markets.” It comes from his January 2015 Lost Tree Club speech. Company fundamentals like revenue, earnings and cash flow matter, as does industry momentum. But liquidity also plays a major role in the multiples investors are willing to pay. $RKLB is executing well, the space industry is gaining serious traction, and money supply is expanding again. Despite some near-term tightening pressures, that’s a much more supportive backdrop for growth stocks. I believe it’s only a matter of time before that gets reflected in RKLB’s valuation.

items.title: $IREN Guys, who would have thought we’d end up here? I’m talking about sentiment toward the entire data center sector, not just IREN. IREN a
items.content_excerpt: $IREN Guys, who would have thought we’d end up here? I’m talking about sentiment toward the entire data center sector, not just IREN. IREN at $21 today—can you imagine? We’re living in a world where demand for AI compute is so huge that companies can’t build enough data centers or secure enough financing to keep up. So much demand, yet such low stock prices. AI is the hottest topic in the world, and without data centers, there is no AI. It’s hard to even imagine how much demand for AI compute there could be over the next five to ten years. $RKLB Congress Changed Hands. Did the $RKLB Thesis Change? I wouldn’t lower expectations for RKLB just because Congress changed hands. Democrats winning doesn’t automatically mean less spending on satellites, hypersonic testing or military launches. Golden Dome funding will require a different set of negotiations, but we need to see actual budget decisions before calling that a setback. Meanwhile, Electron has commercial customers to serve, and existing defense contracts give Rocket Lab work to deliver, although those awards aren’t immune to funding changes. There’s political uncertainty here, but that alone isn’t evidence the business has weakened. For me, the bigger questions remain the same: - Can Electron keep increasing its launch cadence? - Can Rocket Lab deliver its satellite contracts at healthy margins? - And can it get Neutron flying? Those are the developments that would change my view of the business.
